declared_proposition: For every finite nonempty set S of primes q>5 and arbitrary pairs (u_q,v_q) in F_q^2, there is a unique pair (A,B) modulo M=product_(q in S)q^2 such that A=2 and B=3 modulo q and F_q(A)=u_q, F_q(B)=v_q for all q in S, where F_q(x)=(x^(q-1)-1)/q modulo q. Therefore every prescribed finite hit/avoidance pattern for the projective slope [3:5] can be interpolated by fixed integers A,B; finite-prime lift-compatible local data alone cannot determine the canonical pair A=2,B=3.
mathematical_argument: The binomial theorem modulo q^2 gives F_q(a+kq)=F_q(a)-k/a modulo q. Thus the unique lift indices are k_q=2(F_q(2)-u_q) and ell_q=3(F_q(3)-v_q) modulo q. The congruences A=2+k_q q and B=3+ell_q q modulo q^2 have unique simultaneous solutions modulo M by the Chinese remainder theorem. Choosing target pairs on or off [3:5] realizes any finite pattern. The interpolated integers depend on S and the targets, so this does not decide the cross-prime behavior of the canonical fixed representatives 2 and 3.

reproducible_computation.algorithm: mod-q^2 exponentiation, affine lift inversion, and exact pairwise-coprime CRT
reproducible_computation.complexity: O(sum_(q in S) log q) modular multiplications plus quasi-linear big-integer CRT overhead per case

finite_computation_boundary: 4 exact CRT certificates are replayed; the theorem for every finite prime set is algebraic.
logical_limit: CRT constructs integers that depend on the finite prime set; it gives no occurrence, avoidance, or density result for F_q(2),F_q(3) as q varies and does not control Collatz trajectories.

route_decision.discard: deducing the cross-prime behavior of the canonical Fermat-quotient pair from any finite collection of lift-compatible local constraints
parked: statistical extrapolation from interpolated noncanonical representatives
route_decision.retain: distribution information genuinely tied to the same fixed representatives 2 and 3 over an unbounded prime set

claim_boundary: No Collatz proof, divergent orbit, or nontrivial cycle; one exact finite-prime interpolation no-go theorem.
